What is happening with the US job market?

US job openings for June were revised down by -177,000 vacancies, their largest monthly downward revision since November 2025.

This also marks the 3rd consecutive monthly downward revision.

Furthermore, the number of hires for June was revised down by -16,000, while the number of quits was revised lower by -19,000.

At the same time, the number of layoffs and discharges was revised up by +19,000.

As a result, job openings have now been revised down in 38 of the last 43 months.

US labor market data is becoming increasingly difficult to read with confidence.

The US AI infrastructure boom is making history.

There are now ~90 US data centers with more than 100 megawatts (MW) of power in operation, the highest count on record.

This figure is set to more than triple by 2030, to ~280, if all currently planned projects are completed.

Over the same period, tech companies are expected to spend ~$7.0 trillion on data centers.

Meanwhile, Amazon, $AMZN, Microsoft, $MSFT, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Meta, $META, have already signed more than $1.5 trillion in data center leases since the AI boom began, including commitments that have yet to take effect.

The AI buildout is one of the largest capital spending cycles in history.

🇨🇳 #China’s $54b Recap Plan To Bolster Financial Capacity - Shanghai Securities News

➡ The 360 billion yuan ($53.7 billion) capital injection into banks and insurers is meant to strengthen financial institutions’ support for economic growth, rather than a move made under stress or risk.

➡ With ICBC and Agricultural Bank of China joining earlier capital recipients in 2024 and 2025, the program now covers all six of China’s major state-owned banks, extending a recapitalization plan first outlined in 2024, the report said, with their core tier one capital exceeding regulatory requirements.

➡ Stronger capital buffers will allow financial institutions to sustain support for financing demand in technology innovation, industrial upgrading and domestic consumption, supporting a stable financial environment in the five-year plan.

➡ The inclusion of state-owned insurers in the capital injections signals a wider push to strengthen multiple layers of China’s financial system, reflecting their distinct roles in the system.

➡ Recapitalization is primarily aimed at replenishing the financial institutions’ core Tier-1 capital, with Agricultural Bank requiring more capital support due to rapid loan and asset growth, a separate report cited Zeng Gang of local financial research institute known as Tianfu Liyan as saying.

➡ This should also give insurers greater capacity to increase long-term equity investments while strengthening the capital base and market influence of state-owned insurance groups over the longer term, according to Ge Yuxiang, analyst at Zhongtai Securities.

tweets.text:
The US Treasury curve is getting yanked from both ends by two men.

Warsh's Fed drives the short end, with a 60% chance of a rate hike priced in this month. Bessent's Treasury works the long end, doubling buybacks to cap a 30-year yield near 5.25%, the highest since 2007.

When one end trades on the Fed and the other on Treasury supply, the whole curve turns unstable. That volatility leaks out of bonds ($TLT) and into the discount rate under stocks and every trade leveraged off Treasuries.
